name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection and analysis of coordinated link-sharing and inauthentic network behavior on social media platforms, including the CooRnet/CLSB methodology and its successors; the researcher's signature methodological contribution, still central to recent publications and the vera.ai project.

name: Information Disorder
description: Study of disinformation, misinformation and 'fake news' circulation within hybrid media systems, including narrative propagation, deceptive information operations and fact-checking support tools; a long-standing core research line reflected in PROMPT, MINE-FACTS and numerous publications.

name: Generative AI and Synthetic Media Disinformation
description: Emerging strand examining how generative AI is used to produce and scale deceptive content (synthetic images, LLM-generated text) in information operations, and how AI tools can assist detection and countering of disinformation; reflected in recent 2025-2026 publications and the new IA Generativa e Media course.

name: LLMs in Computational Content Analysis
description: Methodological work on integrating and validating Large Language Models within human-in-the-loop pipelines for text classification and annotation in political discourse and communication research, addressing challenges of reliability, disagreement and validation.

name: Platform Governance and Research Data Access
description: Analysis of social media platform policies, moderation/content-reduction decisions, and the shifting landscape of research APIs and data access tools under regulatory regimes like the EU Digital Service Act, including the transition away from CrowdTangle and toward walled-garden platform environments.

name: Political Polarization and Partisan News Ecosystems
description: Research on partisan alignment, insularity, cross-partisan interaction patterns and the amplification of political polarization across social and traditional media, including partisan attention scores and computational political parallelism studies centered on Italian and European elections.

name: Italian Election Media Mapping (MINE)
description: The MINE programme's core empirical line mapping Italian news media and social media coverage across national election cycles (2018, 2019, 2022), studying Facebook/Instagram engagement, hyperpartisan networks and citizen interaction with electoral campaigns; the institutional umbrella for the researcher's ongoing agenda.

name: Health Misinformation Networks
description: Investigation of coordinated networks circulating problematic health information (COVID-19, vaccines, general health content) on social media in Italy, India and Nigeria, examining low-quality sources, ethnic/religious drivers and online gatekeeping by news aggregators.

name: Comparative Digital Media and Elections
description: Cross-national comparative studies of coordinated political advertising, information campaigns and platform dynamics around elections beyond Italy (Germany, Brazil, Latin America, Nigeria), extending the researcher's coordination-detection methods to new electoral and political contexts.

name: Public and Sociotechnical Approaches to AI Safety Evaluation
description: Papers framing AI safety practices—red-teaming and evaluation—as sociotechnical activities requiring public involvement, labor consideration, and participatory science methods rather than purely technical procedures.

name: Online Radicalization and Extremism Across Platforms
description: Empirical and review studies of how extremist actors (far-right, jihadist) exploit platform affordances, algorithms, and multimodal content to spread and normalize radical ideologies online.

name: Retrospective Essays on Platformization and Social Media's Trajectory
description: Reflective anniversary/position essays diagnosing the current state of social media and platform economies, tracing how platformization, political economy, and scam/extractive logics have reshaped online life over the past decade.

name: Public Attitudes and Labor Experiences with AI
description: Survey- and discourse-based studies of how publics and workers perceive, use, and are shaped by AI systems, including stakeholder discourse, national attitudes, and worker-reported productivity and displacement effects.

name: LLMs and Computational Methods for Research Workflows
description: Methodological papers deploying LLMs or fine-tuned models to augment scholarly tasks such as peer review, qualitative coding, and domain-specific classification, with attention to human-in-the-loop design and evaluation.

name: Message-Based Interventions for Climate Communication and Misinformation Resistance
description: Experimental and review studies testing how framed messages, chatbots, or inoculation techniques shape audience attitudes, resistance to misinformation, and engagement with climate or conspiracy content.

name: Survey Data Quality, Comprehension, and Recruitment
description: Papers examining the methodological foundations of online survey research, including whether respondents understand survey questions as intended, how representative and valid different opt-in sample sources are, and how novel platform-based recruitment strategies (e.g., Facebook ads) can be used and evaluated for reaching hard-to-survey populations.

name: Computational Approaches to Social Network Structure and Community Formation
description: Papers developing or applying computational/graph-based methods to detect, map, and explain emergent structural patterns—communities, practice clusters, and transitive ties—in large-scale online social networks, using techniques such as self-supervised graph embeddings and causal network analysis.

name: Cultural Imaginaries and Framings of Generative AI
description: Papers examining how generative AI is culturally imagined, discursively framed, and theorized as a medium, ranging from newspaper coverage and Silicon Valley community discourse to media-theoretical accounts of AI's distinctive properties as a creative medium.
